Parathyroid hormone (PTH) acts on the proximal renal tubules to inhibit the reabsorption of phosphate, often referred to as decreased renal phosphate absorption in this context. This inhibition prevents phosphate from returning to the blood, leading to increased urinary excretion (phosphaturia). Consequently, the net loss of phosphate from the body results in the decreased serum phosphate levels observed in hyperparathyroidism.
